summary: LunaBase: First Light is a browser-based 3D learning game for children aged 7–12. Players become junior astronauts at Asteria Outpost, a fictional lunar research base. They complete guided tasks involving life support, water recovery, solar power, greenhouse growing and crew safety. NASA space-weather and space-biology research provides real scientific context, while the outpost story and simplified resource values remain clearly identified as a training simulation.
details:
LunaBase

About the Project

LunaBase is a browser-based 3D educational game for children aged 7–12. Players take the role of a junior astronaut at Asteria Outpost, a fictional lunar research base, where they explore facilities and learn what it takes to keep a Moon base running.

How It Works

Players complete guided missions involving five essential areas:

  • Life Support: Inspect the air system and respond to equipment problems.
  • Water Recovery: Complete activities to understand how used water can be cleaned and reused.
  • Solar Power: Maintain solar panels and manage available electricity.
  • Greenhouse: Plant crops and manage the water and light needed for growth.
  • Crew Safety: Make decisions during a simulated space-weather emergency.

Players explore the 3D environment, interact with equipment, follow mission instructions and see how their choices affect the base.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project aims to make space science easier and more interesting for young learners. It encourages problem-solving, decision-making and resource awareness by showing how air, water, power, food and crew safety are connected.

NASA Research

We use NASA research to provide real scientific context for selected activities:

  • NASA DONKI: Historical solar-event information supports the space-weather safety lesson.
  • NASA OSDR (OSD-480): Research on plant responses to different gravity conditions supports the greenhouse learning section.
  • NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter: Lunar images and research help inform the Moon environment.

The Asteria Outpost, resource values and mission outcomes are part of an educational simulation, not real NASA measurements or an actual lunar base.

Technology and Creativity

The application is built using React, TypeScript, Three.js, HTML, CSS and Vite. GitHub is used for source-code management, and Vercel hosts the game.

Our creative approach combines 3D exploration with simple engineering activities and resource-management decisions. We considered the age of our audience, ease of use, scientific accuracy and performance on ordinary computers.

Our aim is to help children learn about the challenges of living beyond Earth through exploration and practical activities rather than reading explanations alone.
